summary: The lecture covers the historical underpinnings of the Indian Constitution focusing on three key British-era acts: Regulating Act 1773, Amending Act 1781, and Pitts India Act 1784. It explains how East India Company's trade monopoly evolved into territorial power after Battles of Plassey and Buxar, leading to Diwani rights over Bengal, Bihar, Orissa. The acts progressively centralized administration, established Supreme Court in Calcutta, created dual governance (Board of Control and Court of Directors), and introduced key concepts like 'British possessions in India' and Governor General's veto power.
points: Indian Polity weightage: 18-24 questions (~40 marks) in UPSC Prelims out of 100 questions.
Constitution framed in 2 years 11 months 18 days; provisions rooted in pre-existing British laws, not made from scratch.
East India Company got trade monopoly via Royal Charter; paid ~46.1 million pounds annually (~460 crore rupees).
Regulating Act 1773: Governor of Bengal became Governor General of Bengal (not India); Supreme Court established at Calcutta (1774).
1773 Act: Supreme Court judges appointed by Crown, not Governor General; jurisdiction only over British subjects, not natives.
Amending Act 1781: Supreme Court barred from revenue matters; British subjects/employees exempted; appellate jurisdiction moved to Governor General in Council.
Pitts India Act 1784: Dual Government - Court of Directors (commercial) and Board of Control (political, 6 members headed by Secretary of State).
1784 Act: 'British possessions in India' phrase first used; Governor General's Council reduced to 3 + Commander-in-Chief; veto power granted.
Madras and Bombay presidencies made subordinate to Bengal; Calcutta became capital under 1784 Act.
Governor General served two masters (Company and Crown) due to unclear boundaries between Board of Control and Court of Directors.

check.q: Under which Act was the Supreme Court established at Calcutta and who appointed its judges?
opts: Regulating Act 1773; Governor General of Bengal

check.q: Which Act first used the phrase 'British possessions in India' and created the Board of Control?
What was the key change in Governor General's Council under Pitts India Act 1784?
opts: Strength increased to 5 members with no veto
Strength reduced to 3 members plus Commander-in-Chief with veto power
Strength reduced to 3 members with consensus-based decisions
Strength kept at 4 members but legislative powers removed
